claims.text: The starting material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic, ordered single-phase hexagonal FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy-alloy film.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films exhibit a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films have high hysteretic losses.
The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis are governed primarily by the distribution of residual stresses and defect-induced local magnetic anisotropies.
Dislocations, grain boundaries, and locally ordered defect clusters, together with residual stress, produce heterogeneous magnetic anisotropy.
These microstructural features pin magnetic domain boundaries at the magnetostructural transition.
A moderate, short-duration rapid thermal anneal can reduce residual stress and defect density without changing the overall phase.
Reducing residual stress and defect density through RTA diminishes domain-wall pinning.
Reduced domain-wall pinning mitigates abrupt nucleation and propagation of domain reversal during the magnetostructural transition.
RTA-treated films will have a broader magnetostructural transition than the as-deposited baseline.
RTA-treated films will have reduced thermal and magnetic hysteresis, observable as a smaller cooling–warming temperature difference and smaller M-H loop area.
Transition broadening and hysteresis reduction will occur without significantly diminishing the magnetocaloric entropy change.
The RTA treatment will improve heat-exchange rates relative to the as-deposited films.
The predicted behavior applies to similarly deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type films during magnetic cycling below approximately 0.2 T.
Competing magnetic interactions involving Fe and Mn may modulate the response.
